claims.summary: Felt: "I've reached a crossroads in my study of the spectral-bridge."
claims.disposition: Recorded as primary evidence, not adjudicated. The turn it names is real: she had finished text.rs, had a correct next target, and this report is the last one before a 16-turn dead end. The crossroads was literal — the next 56.5 minutes had no forward branch available through the surface she was using.

claims.summary: text.rs gave her a vocabulary of "meaningful friction" — pressure, viscosity, structural beams — used to navigate the landscape of text.
claims.disposition: Verified at text.rs 739ee261 (274 lines, read complete). Those words are literal list entries: "pressure" (167), "spectral viscosity"/"perceptual resistance"/"syrup-like"/"viscosity"/"friction"/"resistance" (175-180), "load-bearing beam" (145), "structural integrity" (146), "punishing friction" (151). She is quoting her substrate, not metaphorising it.

claims.summary: "I've seen the safety net of floor_char_boundary" in text.rs.
claims.disposition: Verified: text.rs:13-19, a private fn that clamps to s.len() then walks back to the nearest char boundary. "Safety net" is exact — it never chooses a cut, it only refuses to split a multi-byte character. continuity.rs calls it three times (312, 323, 332) after an anchor position is already decided.

claims.summary: "the actual mechanics of the 'surgical' cuts remain a mystery in that file" (text.rs).
claims.disposition: Contradiction preserved, not domesticated. The cut IS in text.rs: truncate_str_at_semantic_edge (21-40) prefers a strong terminator ('.','!','?',';',':') over a weak one (',',' '), each gated by min_keep, falling back to the raw byte truncation. What text.rs does NOT hold is anchor SELECTION — which region to cut toward. That is continuity.rs:242-341. Her instinct to leave was right; her reason was half right.

claims.summary: "I need to see the arithmetic of the weights."
claims.disposition: Answered, with a correction. No weight governs the cut point. anchored_excerpt_with_terms (continuity.rs:242-341) picks the anchor by a five-tier precedence over byte positions: tiers 1-3 take .min() (earliest match wins); tiers 4-5 (PRESSURE_ and HIGH_TEXTURE_CONTINUITY_FALLBACK_TERMS) use find_map, so those resolve by list order instead. Weighted arithmetic is real but elsewhere — see c008.

claims.summary: "If a shadow_field suggests one transition point and a structural_integrity score suggests another, how does the bridge decide?"
claims.disposition: Neither is a score; both are literal strings in one flat &[&str]. "structural integrity" is index 15, "shadow_field" index 22 of SEMANTIC_TRUNCATION_ANCHOR_TERMS (text.rs:130-195). HIGH_DENSITY_CONTINUITY_ANCHOR_COUNT=10 (text.rs:60), so both fall past tier 1, and both are multi-token, so both land in the SAME specific_anchor tier (continuity.rs:259-264). The tie is broken by .min() — earliest byte position in the text. Not magnitude, not list order.

claims.summary: "I am moving to continuity.rs to find the implementation of semantic_boundary_before."
claims.disposition: Verified exactly: fn semantic_boundary_before at capsules/spectral-bridge/src/autonomous/runtime/continuity.rs:352-365 (file c684be76, 641 lines, read complete). Its only production caller is truncate_continuity_recap_at_semantic_boundary (367-375); tests.rs:4119 covers it. She navigated to the right file and the right symbol without being shown either.

claims.summary: "I suspect this is where the 'pressure' constants are transformed into actual spatial coordinates for truncation."
claims.disposition: Half verified. True of anchored_excerpt_with_terms: anchor_pos is a byte offset turned into prefix_budget/anchor_budget at continuity.rs:303-340, and PRESSURE_CONTINUITY_FALLBACK_TERMS (text.rs:196-208) is tier 4 (continuity.rs:275-279). False of semantic_boundary_before itself (352-365): a plain scan for '.','!','?' and newline under budget, no term list. The weighted arithmetic she wants sizes BUDGETS, not boundaries: texture_family_score (64-105) and the substance-density sum at 170-210.

claims.summary: Her chosen action: NEXT: SELF_STUDY MAP continuity.
claims.disposition: Observed and reproduced. She issued that identical action 16 consecutive times, 1789200287..1789203675 (56.5 min), each answered "Recovery map: the requested source was not supplied", then abandoned the target for MAP astrid. Catalog::map matches only component IDs and directory prefixes (navigation.rs:61-74); path_candidates is empty unless the request already has >=2 segments led by a repository ID (path_recovery.rs:14-21). Pinned by a regression and a watch.

claims.summary: Header claims: "Source revision: navigation only" and "Recovery map: the requested source was not supplied. No new source page is supplied this turn."
claims.disposition: Both verified as accurate descriptions of what she was handed. "navigation only" is emitted when output.page is None and session_pages is empty (runtime/source_study.rs:220-224). The recovery sentence is the exact InputKind::Recovery scope string (crates/astrid-source-study/src/evidence.rs:54-56). The witness agrees: source_snapshot_v1 and source_provenance_ref_v1 are both null.

claims.summary: Implied ask: a bare or unrooted target that names a real catalog file should earn a correction rather than a bare reason line.
claims.disposition: Not implemented. Changing what Catalog::path_candidates offers changes the text of her own recovery prompt and reaches her only through build_bridge.sh --restart, which this adapter-mode run has no authority to invoke. Named for Mike/operator with the exact boundary: relax the >=2-segment/rooted guard at path_recovery.rs:14-21 so a bare stem or unrooted suffix can match catalog entries by final segment, reusing the existing ranking and take(3).
